newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: IMF's Fischer to meet Uzbek leader in May.
newsitem.headline: IMF's Fischer to meet Uzbek leader in May.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund is to send a high-ranking official to Uzbekistan next month to try to patch strained relations with the former Soviet republic, an Uzbek official said on Wednesday.

The official, who liaises with international lending institutions but who declined to be named, said the fund's deputy managing director, Stanley Fischer, will meet Uzbek President Islam Karimov at the latter's invitation on May 2.

"One of the IMF's highest officials will visit the Uzbek capital to discuss with President Islam Karimov the current economic situation and prospects for further cooperation between the fund and Uzbekistan," he said.
The IMF suspended a $185 million standby loan to Uzbekistan late last year, saying the resource-rich country of 23 million people had failed to meet the fund's inflation targets.
The official said the invitation was aimed at improving relations with the fund.
Both the IMF and the World Bank have criticised the republic's foreign exchange controls.
The government, desperate for cash to bail out Uzbekistan's troubled agriculture sector, imposed the controls following poor cotton and grain harvests in 1996.
In December, Karimov put paid to rumours that Uzbekistan might reintroduce currency convertibility this year, saying he would not subject the republic to "slavery" under the IMF.

There is now a wide difference between the official and black market exchange rates for Uzbekistan's sum currency. The Central Bank officially traded 59.50 sums to the dollar on Wednesday versus the black market rate of 145 sums to the dollar from money changers in the silk route country's bazaars.
Fischer's visit also coincides with a routine IMF mission to the republic which begins on Thursday and which will last until May 13.
